maturity.title: Recording and transcription
maturity.subtitle: F9 and the visible record control start, stop, and finalize ordinary dictation.

maturity.title: Recording setup controls
maturity.subtitle: Language, microphone, function key, and recording behavior can be adjusted before capture.

maturity.title: History
maturity.subtitle: Completed captures remain visible and recoverable in the local History surface.

maturity.title: Custom saved styles
maturity.subtitle: A user-created writing style can be selected and applied to dictated text.

maturity.title: Rewrite conversations
maturity.subtitle: Originals, Quick Polish, Structured Note, follow-ups and conversation export form the daily Omarchy workspace.

maturity.title: Editable documents and automatic copy
maturity.subtitle: Originals and rewrites can be edited, saved and copied automatically in the Omarchy workflow.

maturity.title: Omarchy recording widget
maturity.subtitle: The themed widget, completed-note rewrites and opening the workspace are used daily on Omarchy.

maturity.title: Screenshot context and narrated annotations
maturity.subtitle: Omarchy region capture, visual AI context and spoken Tensaku text boxes passed isolated checks; physical-key and microphone acceptance remain pending.

maturity.title: Independent rewrite and speech providers
maturity.subtitle: Compatible APIs and app-owned local models have controlled checks; cloud accounts need acceptance.

maturity.title: Live structured rewriting
maturity.subtitle: Opt-in task, note, polish and custom drafts expose missing information; model quality needs acceptance.

maturity.title: Automatic paste
maturity.subtitle: Known limitation: insertion is disabled by default and depends on the target application and desktop; clipboard delivery is the standard workflow.

maturity.title: Faithful cleanup
maturity.subtitle: Optional Codex cleanup preserves the raw transcript and falls back safely, but still needs manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Spoken structure
maturity.subtitle: Punctuation, paragraph, and scratch-that commands still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Command mode
maturity.subtitle: Spoken editing instructions are previewed before delivery and still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Notes mode
maturity.subtitle: Longer acceptance-gated drafts and their relaunch recovery still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Meeting mode
maturity.subtitle: Microphone plus system-audio capture, diarization, review, and archive still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Shell menu and recording bar
maturity.subtitle: The optional GNOME Shell menu and display-only bottom bar have off-screen evidence but still need live-desktop acceptance.

maturity.title: Dictionary and vocabulary suggestions
maturity.subtitle: Local replacements and review-only suggestions still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Snippets
maturity.subtitle: Explicit spoken expansions and portable typed-trigger storage still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Per-application memory and context
maturity.subtitle: Remembered modes, styles, rules, and bounded context controls still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Advanced recovery, retention, and Incognito
maturity.subtitle: Retries, reprocessing, exports, retention policies, and Incognito still need manual acceptance.

maturity.title: Diagnostics export
maturity.subtitle: Privacy-safe timing diagnostics still need manual acceptance.

mode.title: Capture mode
mode.tooltip:
Dictate: press the configured global function key to start and again to finish.
Command (Experimental): review a spoken edit or drafting instruction before delivery.
Notes (Experimental): keep a longer editable draft until you copy or delete it.
Meeting (Experimental): use the separate Meeting tab for explicit microphone and system-audio capture.

language.title: Transcription language
language.subtitle: Auto-detect lets the selected speech provider choose the language

global_recording_key.title: Recording key
global_recording_key.subtitle: F13–F24 typically have the fewest conflicts but usually need a programmable keyboard layer; F9 is the practical default on a standard keyboard
global_recording_key.tooltip: Press once to start and again to stop. F1–F12 may already be used by applications, desktop features, or keyboard firmware. F13–F24 are usually least used but are absent from most standard keyboards.

system_audio_device.title: Meeting system output · Experimental
system_audio_device.subtitle: Meeting captures all audio playing through the selected sink

remember_application_switch.title: Remember mode and style per application · Experimental
remember_application_switch.subtitle: Uses a local executable identity that is never sent to Codex

automatic_titles_switch.title: Automatic conversation titles
automatic_titles_switch.subtitle: Send an excerpt of each new conversation to the rewrite provider for a title. A local label is used if unavailable.

spoken_commands_switch.title: Spoken structure · Experimental
spoken_commands_switch.subtitle: Apply explicit punctuation, new line, new paragraph, and scratch-that commands

incognito_switch.title: Incognito · Experimental
incognito_switch.subtitle: New sessions write no local history or recovery audio. Recognition uses your selected speech provider.

cases.latest: Shift+F9 needs desktop approval. The shell menu also opens your latest dictation.
